symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1597 (case B): `@annotation('Why this commit is here.')` in an `alter microflow … insert after $Result begin … end;` fragment passed check and exec ("Altered microflow") and no note was written; the same line in `create or modify microflow` is refused as MDL079
cause: the annotation rules (MDL059 unknown name, MDL060 bad curve, MDL079 bad note, MDL092 bad anchor) ran only over create bodies — ValidateProgram had no AlterFlowStmt case, and execAlterFlow ran no statement validation — while the fragment goes through the same flowBuilder, which drops what the visitor could not read
file: mdl/executor/validate_alter_flow.go (ValidateAlterFlow, validateAlterFlowRules); validate_program.go (AlterFlowStmt case); cmd_alter_flow.go (execAlterFlow refuses the exec-enforced subset before loading)
test: TestValidateProgram_ChecksAnnotationsInAnAlterFlowFragment (all four rules, insert and replace, nested in an if), TestValidateProgram_AlterFlowFragmentValidNotesStayClean (control), TestExecAlterFlow_RefusesADroppedAnnotation
insight: The reported rule was one of four with the same hole: probing `@postion`, `@curve(from: (a, b))` and `@anchor(from: sideways)` in the same fragment showed all four passing, which is what moved the fix from one rule to walkAnnotations. Only the annotation rules are run on a fragment — the rest of the microflow rule set reads parameters, declares and later uses of the whole flow, which a fragment cannot see, so running ValidateMicroflow on it would trade a silent drop for false refusals. MDL079 is still not exec-enforced for create or alter, so `-c` and the REPL write past it in both; exec of a file is covered by its check preflight
